attr.attrdef: The two-character identification code assigned to each area polygon by the Boise Police Department. The Boise Police categorize areas into two generic locales, Valley and Bench. The first character identifies which one of the two locales the beat is assigned to; ‘V’ corresponds to Valley administrative districts, ‘B’ corresponds to Bench administrative districts.

dataIdInfo.idPurp:
This data set was created for Boise City Police Department administrative and reporting functions. The data delineates jurisdictional boundaries for police officials to: 1) verify paperwork; 2) use for planning; 3) generate crime statistics; and 4) utilize in the county police records management system.
Spatial data sets representing police areas exist for neighboring agencies including the Ada County Sheriff’s Office (ACSO), Garden City Police Department (GCPD), and Meridian Police Department (MPD). This data set also has a relationship to the BPD_Divisions (the largest territorial police boundaries) and BPD_ReportingDistricts (smallest territorial police boundaries) data sets which serve similar functions. However, the internal boundaries and are different. See the metadata for BPD_Divisions and BPD_ReportingDistricts for more information.
This data set also bears similarity to the Ada County Police Atoms which are designed expressly for the dispatch of emergency responders. The county police atoms aggregate additional geometry and attributes not applicable to the purpose and function of this data set.
dataIdInfo.idAbs:
This is a polygon data set representing the current Boise City Police (BPD) areas. Police areas are the second to largest division of territorial boundaries used by law enforcement to deploy manpower, organize officers below their senior commanders, and to track reported crimes, accidents, and calls for service. Police areas are an aggregate of smaller jurisdictional boundaries called reporting districts.

Boise City Police areas exist only within the Boise City limits. This data set was created by Boise City GIS; it was derived by aggregating groups of reporting districts as determined by the Boise Police Department. It is current to the date it was published.
